items.title: How fast do orphaned components pile up when governance stops running?
items.description: Northwind's own numbers: with active governance, roughly 2 new orphaned components accumulate per year (things get caught and retired close to when they stop being used). Once the review process lapses (as it did after Northwind's year-3 reorg), unreviewed orphans pile up far faster per year of the gap. Drag the slider to see how many orphaned components you'd expect after a governance gap of a given length, compared against what the same period would have produced under active governance — Northwind's real gap was 18 months.
items.compute: const monthsToYears = params.gapMonths / 12; const withGovernance = monthsToYears * 2; const withoutGovernance = monthsToYears * 11; const orphans = Math.round(withoutGovernance); return { orphans, wouldHaveBeen: Math.round(withGovernance) };

outputs.label: Orphaned components (would have been, with governance)

items.title: What review capacity does an org actually need to keep the 30-day resolution rate healthy?
items.description: Northwind's centralized team of 3 kept 88% of exceptions resolved within 30 days at 40 screens (about 13 screens per reviewer), but the same 3-person team only managed 41% once the org reached 340 screens (about 113 screens per reviewer). Drag the slider to see the expected resolution rate for a given screens-per-reviewer ratio.
items.compute: const rate = Math.max(8, Math.round(88 - (params.screensPerReviewer - 13) * 0.47)); return { rate };
